subject: Circle USDC and Ripple RLUSD supply/liquidity on XRPL, Circle global issuance and Coinbase distribution economics

xrpl_tokens.indexer_note: XRPLWin states WinDB follows the ledger by a few minutes. The page says current supply/holder values are exact according to its indexer, while historical supply/holder series are reconstructed from daily balances. Raw XRPL account_lines/gateway_balances were not independently queried in this run.

comparisons.caveat: Same-indexer comparison. Account-level top-holder concentration does not establish beneficial-owner concentration; 24h sent/payment values are not verified external commerce or net capital flows.

circle_global_usdc.interpretation: Circle-reported global circulation contracted over the preceding 30 days. This is issuer-level net redemption, not evidence of rotation into XRP or any other cryptoasset.

circle_q2_2026_sec.reserve_income_yield_sensitivity: Circle attributed approximately $113.9M of Q2 reserve-income growth offset to a 66bp decline in average yields, while higher average daily USDC circulation contributed approximately $147.4M of increase.
circle_q2_2026_sec.caveat: Company filing data; USDC on Coinbase platform includes corporate-held and non-custodial balances under Circle's definition, not only customer custodial assets.

management_commentary: Average USDC held on Coinbase products reached an all-time high
Coinbase renewed its Circle arrangement on the same terms
DEX trading and balances borrowed/lent through Coinbase grew
coinbase_q3_2026_sec.interpretation: Coinbase's strategic mix is shifting toward stablecoins, derivatives, onchain trading and credit while spot volumes and transacting users declined. Q3 net income is not equivalent to underlying trading strength because $715.0M of investment-asset gains largely explains the result.

hypotheses.statement: Circle has a direct XRPL presence through native USDC, but its current XRPL supply is small relative to global USDC and to RLUSD on XRPL.
hypotheses.counter_evidence: XRPLWin indexer data is not raw RPC reproduction; current supply and pools can change.

hypotheses.statement: Ripple RLUSD has substantially greater XRPL token supply and deeper RLUSD/XRP AMM liquidity than Circle USDC/XRP.
hypotheses.counter_evidence: Pool reserves are point-in-time and not executable depth; beneficial-owner attribution and full market coverage are unknown.

hypotheses.statement: The XRPL RLUSD/USDC AMM pool creates a permissionless conversion route between Ripple and Circle stablecoins.
hypotheses.counter_evidence: Pool size and 30-day trade count are small; no formal Circle-Ripple partnership is implied.

hypotheses.statement: Circle's 30-day net USDC redemption could reflect weakening stablecoin demand.
hypotheses.counter_evidence: Redemptions may reflect treasury reallocation, seasonal settlement, rate expectations or market-maker inventory; no link to XRP rotation is evidenced.

hypotheses.statement: Circle's earnings are highly exposed to reserve balances and interest rates, while Coinbase is a financially material distribution partner.
hypotheses.counter_evidence: Circle is expanding Arc, USYC, CPN and StableFX; product diversification may reduce long-run dependence.

hypotheses.statement: Coinbase is diversifying away from dependence on spot trading toward stablecoin distribution, derivatives, DEX and credit products.
hypotheses.counter_evidence: Spot volume weakness may be cyclical; it does not prove permanent structural decline or XRP-specific weakness.

hypotheses.statement: Stablecoins on XRPL may complement XRP liquidity while also substituting for XRP as a bridge in some settlement routes.
hypotheses.counter_evidence: No corridor-level or AMM flow decomposition establishes substitution or complementarity at scale.

model_controls.reason: Indexer observations lack raw RPC reproduction and historical point-in-time series; issuer and SEC metrics are not XRP directional features without causal validation.
